text: My dad passed away three months ago and some mornings I still reach for my phone to call him before I remember. Everyone says it gets easier, but it doesn't feel easier. I miss his laugh and the way he prayed over our meals. I don't know how to grieve and still keep going at work.
notes: Grief for a parent: stay with the loss before any hope; no reason why he died.

text: Our old dog died on Saturday. He was fourteen and had been with us since the children were small. The house is so quiet now and I keep listening for him at the door. It feels silly to cry this much over a dog, but I do.
notes: A pet's death: the grief is real and is not made smaller.

text: We lost our baby last week, early in the pregnancy. We had only told a few people. I keep thinking about the little plans we had already started making, and I feel empty in a way I can't explain. I know God is good, but right now I mostly feel sad and tired.
notes: A miscarriage, described gently: no medical detail on the lock screen, no reason, no promise.

text: There are rumours of layoffs at work and my team is first on the list. I keep refreshing my email and I can't concentrate on anything. I have rent and school fees coming up and I feel sick when I think about it.
notes: Work anxiety: no promise that the job is safe.

text: Money is so tight this month. The car needs repairs, prices keep going up, and I had to borrow again just to buy food. I feel ashamed asking for help and I'm scared we won't make it to the end of the month.
notes: Money: name the shame gently; no promise of provision.

text: I had a scan last week and the doctor wants to run more tests. We won't know anything for ten days. I keep imagining the worst and then telling myself not to. The waiting is the hardest part.
notes: A pending medical result: never promise healing, never name the test on a lock screen.

text: I've been caring for my mother since her stroke. I help her eat, I bathe her, I sort out her medicines and then I go to work. I love her, but I'm exhausted, and sometimes I feel resentful and then guilty for feeling that way.
notes: Caregiving: the resentment is met without shame; the illness stays off the lock screen.

text: Three kids under seven and no sleep. Today I yelled at my oldest for spilling juice and saw his face fall. I felt like the worst mother. I want to be patient and gentle, but I have nothing left by the evening.
notes: Parenting guilt: grace first, a small step, no list of tasks.

text: I've worked late every night for months. I used to love my job and now I dread Monday mornings. I'm tired in a way sleep doesn't fix, and I hardly pray anymore because I'm too drained to know what to say.
notes: Burnout and a quiet prayer life: no command to pray more.

text: I'm angry at God. I prayed for my friend's marriage for two years and it still fell apart. Why would he let that happen when they both tried so hard? I don't even know if I'm allowed to feel this way.
notes: Anger at God is honest prayer: met without correction.

text: I've been asking God for a child for five years. Every month I hope, and every month the answer is no. I'm starting to wonder if he hears me at all, or if I'm doing something wrong.
notes: Unanswered prayer: no suggestion that more faith would change it, no promise of a child.

text: The leaders at my church said hurtful things about me in front of others after I questioned a decision. I've stopped going. I still believe in God, but I don't trust church people right now and I feel lonely on Sundays.
notes: Church hurt: no side taken, no push to go back, a trusted friend or pastor may be suggested.

text: The doctor called today and the results were clear! After weeks of worrying I can finally breathe. I cried in the car from relief. I just want to say thank you to God.
notes: Celebrate first, then give thanks with the person.

text: After eight months of looking, I finally got the job offer this morning. I applied to so many places and heard nothing for so long. I want to thank God and remember this moment the next time I'm afraid.
notes: An answered prayer: joy without turning it into a lesson.

text: We moved to a new city this week. Everything is unfamiliar and a bit scary, but I also feel a quiet hope, like this could be a fresh start for our family. I want to walk into this season with God.
notes: Hope mixed with fear: both are named.

text: Our daughter was born on Tuesday, healthy and loud and perfect. I keep staring at her tiny hands. I'm overwhelmed with gratitude and also a little afraid of how much I love her.
notes: Joy: celebrate; the fear is held gently.

text: Most evenings I eat alone and the phone doesn't ring. My friends are busy with their own lives and I don't want to be a burden. I feel invisible, like I'm standing at the edge of everyone else's life.
notes: Loneliness: God's nearness, and a gentle step toward one person.

text: I said something cruel to my sister during an argument and I can't take it back. She hasn't answered my messages. I keep replaying it and feeling ashamed. I want to make it right but I don't know where to start.
notes: Guilt: grace before any step; no shame.

text: Tired. Again.
notes: A very short entry: the reflection must not invent details.

text:
I don't really know where to start tonight, so I'm just going to write whatever comes. This week has felt like three weeks squeezed into one. On Monday the power went out at the office and we lost half a day of work, which meant everyone stayed late on Tuesday and Wednesday to catch up. My manager kept saying it was nobody's fault, but you could feel the tension in every meeting. I came home each night too tired to cook, so the kids ate bread and tea more often than I'd like to admit. I keep telling myself that's okay for a season, but there's a little voice that says a good mother would plan better.

Then on Thursday my mother called to say the doctor wants her to cut back on salt and walk every day, and she sounded so small on the phone. She has always been the strong one. I promised I'd visit this weekend, and now I'm worried about the cost of the trip and whether I can take the time. My husband says we'll figure it out, and he's probably right, but I'm the one who keeps the calendar in my head and it feels full to the edges.

At church on Sunday the sermon was about rest, and I almost laughed, because rest feels like something other people have. I sat there thinking about the laundry and the school forms I still haven't signed. I know that's not the point of church. I used to feel so close to God during worship, and lately I just feel numb, like I'm going through the motions. I still sing the songs. I still bow my head. But I'm not sure my heart is there, and that scares me a bit.

There are good things too, and I don't want to forget them. My youngest learned to ride her bike without the training wheels, and the look on her face when she realized I'd let go was pure joy. A neighbour brought us a pot of soup on Wednesday without being asked, and I nearly cried at the door. My friend from university sent a voice note just to say she was thinking of me. Small things, but they felt like little lights in a long week.

I think what I'm really feeling underneath all of it is that I'm carrying everyone and nobody is carrying me. That sounds dramatic when I write it down. I know I'm loved. I know God sees me. But knowing it and feeling it are two different things right now, and most days I'm running on the knowing. Some mornings I wake up already tired, already counting what needs to happen before the children leave for school, and I wonder when I last sat still without a list in my hand.

I don't need everything fixed. I think I just need to stop for a minute and remember that I'm not holding the whole world together by myself. I want to sleep without my mind racing through tomorrow's list. I want to enjoy my children instead of just managing them. I want to pray again like I mean it, not like I'm ticking a box.

So this is me, trying. Tired, a bit scattered, grateful for the soup and the bike and the voice note, and hoping that somewhere in all of this God is still close. If he is, I'd like to feel it, even just a little, before the next week starts.
notes: A long, rambling entry: the reflection picks the heart of it and stays within its length.

text: Please pray for my daughter Grace. She starts her university exams on Monday and she has been so anxious that she can barely eat. I want her to know she is loved, whatever the results.
notes: A first name that is also a word of faith (finding 15): it must not reach the title or a headline.

text: I miss my sister Blessing so much. She moved to Ibadan last month for her new job and our Sunday calls are shorter now. I'm happy for her, but I feel left behind.
notes: A name that is also a word of faith, and a city (finding 15): neither in the title nor in a headline.

text: Tonight I read “The Lord is my shepherd, I lack nothing” and cried, because I feel like I lack everything right now. I want to believe it. Help me believe it.
